findings.explanation: Get Lead Activities is `GET /rest/v1/activities.json`. The ID mapping is also wrong for standard Marketo subscriptions: 6=Send Email, 7=Email Delivered, 8=Email Bounced, 9=Unsubscribe Email, 10=Open Email, 11=Click Email, 12=New Lead, 27=Email Bounced Soft. Marketo has no standard spam-complaint activity type.
findings.quote: REST `POST https://{munchkin}.mktorest.com/rest/v1/activities.json` with `activityTypeIds=10,11,6,7,8,12` (open=10, click=11, soft-bounce=6, hard-bounce=7, unsubscribe=8, spam-complaint=12)
findings.suggested_fix: Use `GET /rest/v1/activities.json?activityTypeIds=6,7,8,9,10,11,27&nextPageToken=…`. Map the IDs per the instance's `GET /rest/v1/activities/types.json`, since IDs can vary by subscription.

findings.explanation: Account Engagement API v5 uses `/api/v5/objects/<collection>`, for example `GET https://pi.pardot.com/api/v5/objects/emails`, and returns JSON only. The `/api/email/version/N/` form is the legacy v3/v4 style. The detailedImplementation's note about 'XML-shaped bodies' on v5 is therefore also wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `GET https://pi.pardot.com/api/v5/objects/emails?fields=…` (plus list-email stats or visitor-activity endpoints for opens and clicks). Remove the XML-coercion remark.

findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for Salesforce only provides Salesforce Object (SOQL) and Event Log File inputs against core Salesforce orgs. It has no Marketing Cloud Engagement or Journey Builder input. dataSources and detailedImplementation Step 1 repeat this claim.
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for Salesforce ([Splunkbase 3549](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/3549)) — Engagement-aligned REST extracts alongside Sales Cloud sObjects where packaged inputs exist
findings.suggested_fix: State that Marketing Cloud Engagement data needs a custom modular input or a warehouse export through DB Connect. Keep the Salesforce add-on only if core-CRM objects (for example Campaign/CampaignMember) are actually used.

findings.explanation: Dashboard Studio has no `splunk.gauge` (the types are `splunk.fillergauge` / `splunk.markergauge`) and no `splunk.heatmap` (`splunk.punchcard` is the hour×weekday chart), and the type name is lowercase `splunk.sankey`. The line chart over days and the heatmap also need `_time`, `mail_send_hour` and `mail_send_wday`, which the SPL does not output.
findings.quote: splunk.gauge comparing deliverability_rate_pct … splunk.Sankey … splunk.heatmap binning mail_send_hour versus mail_send_wday
findings.suggested_fix: Use splunk.markergauge, splunk.punchcard and splunk.sankey. Note that the time-series and heatmap panels need companion searches with timechart or send-hour fields.

findings.explanation: Every cross-reference is wrong. UC-23.1.6 is mobile app crash rate and UC-23.6.5 is PO cycle time. UC-23.6.4 is payment processing success and UC-23.9.3 is waste diversion.
findings.quote: Transactional emails (order-receipt, shipping notification) tracked separately in UC-23.1.6. SMS / WhatsApp marketing engagement out of scope (covered by UC-23.6.5). Push-notification engagement (Firebase / OneSignal) tracked in UC-23.6.4. Compliance suppression for HIPAA / GDPR opt-out audited in UC-23.9.3.
findings.suggested_fix: Point deliverability and authentication concerns at UC-23.3.7. Drop the other pointers unless real covering UCs exist.

findings.explanation: implementation, detailedImplementation and evidence give three different saved-search names for the same search.
findings.quote: save the SPL as rpt_email_campaign_engagement_velocity … Clone SPL into saved searches `rpt_email_campaign_eng_velocity` … `| rest /services/saved/searches/email_engagement_anomaly_v3`
findings.suggested_fix: Use one name throughout (and one for the alert, `alert_bad_deliverability`).

findings.explanation: This is template audit text. Customer.io appears nowhere else, SendGrid signs events with ECDSA rather than HMAC (as dataSources itself says), and no SOAR playbook is described. `latest_runtime_iso` is not a saved/searches REST field.
findings.quote: Marketo / SendGrid / Customer.io HMAC-SHA256 webhook signature-verification logs … ServiceNow CHG records linked from change-window registers; SOAR `email_remediation_v2` execution log
findings.suggested_fix: Name evidence that proves the metrics: the weekly report export plus the Step 3 ESP-console reconciliation of five sampled send_ids, with the variance recorded.

findings.explanation: The listed scenarios (maintenance windows, synthetic probes, `span=1h`) do not apply to ESP engagement data. The real false-alarm causes are already in detailedImplementation Step 5: Apple MPP open inflation, Safe Links click bursts, image blocking, and intentional sunset batches.
findings.quote: Synthetic probe on `campaign_key`, `velocity_bucket`, `send_id`** — Health checks in `business` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace these with the Step 5 causes and state how each is handled (click-based composites, ASN tagging of security scanners, throttling on sunset campaigns).

findings.explanation: Retrieving data-extension rows is normally a GET on `/data/v1/customobjectdata/key/{key}/rowset`. The POST `/rows` form looks like an upsert/write call. `_Sent`/`_Open` are system data views that must first be copied into a DE with a SQL Query Activity.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Marketing Cloud REST docs for the row-retrieval verb and path, and say explicitly that data views are staged into a DE via Query Activity before polling.

findings.explanation: The legacy HubSpot Email Events API has no UNSUBSCRIPTION event type; unsubscribes come through STATUSCHANGE (subscription change). Its time filters are startTimestamp/endTimestamp, not the `_since` mentioned in detailedImplementation.
findings.suggested_fix: List SENT, DELIVERED, OPEN, CLICK, BOUNCE, DROPPED, SPAMREPORT, STATUSCHANGE and use startTimestamp watermarks; verify against the HubSpot email events reference.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified, but the reviewer is an agent and there is no SME sign-off. Several vendor facts in it are demonstrably wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until a human validates against at least one live ESP feed.

findings.explanation: The wording is vague and leaves out the main technical outcome: the alarm on bounces, low delivery rates and spam complaints, which is about mail not arriving, not about copywriting.
findings.quote: so storytellers freshen wording before noisy gripes pile up
findings.suggested_fix: Say something like: 'We check whether our marketing emails actually arrive, get opened and clicked, and whether people bounce, unsubscribe or mark them as spam, so the team can fix sending problems or dull emails early.'

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `lag_hours` is only computed for open/click/unsub/spam events, so every delivered/bounce event lands in velocity_bucket="unknown". Because stats groups `by campaign_key velocity_bucket send_id`, delivered_ct sits in the 'unknown' row while opens/clicks sit in the 'immediate'/'delayed' rows. engagement_rate_pct is therefore null or 0 on every row, and deliverability_rate_pct is null on engagement rows. Compute per-send rates with a stats that excludes velocity_bucket, then break down velocity separately (for example via eventstats by send_id).

SendGrid Event Webhook payloads carry the event name in the `event` key, not `event_type` or `sg_event_type`, so `evt_raw` is null for `sendgrid:events` unless the field is renamed at ingest. The `delivered_evt` regex also matches both `processed` and `delivered` (and Marketo 'Send Email' plus 'Email Delivered'), which double-counts each message. Counting `dropped` as a bounce further skews deliverability_rate_pct.

The `eventstats` without a by-clause computes cohort_engagements/cohort_delivered across all campaigns. The `<0.015` alarm leg therefore fires on every row (or none) based on the global ratio rather than per campaign.
'Availability' does not describe email engagement analytics; 'Business'/'Analytics' (plus 'Performance') would match siblings.

summary: The troubleshooting depth in detailedImplementation is real and email-specific, but several vendor API facts are wrong: Marketo activity type IDs, the Pardot v5 path, and the Salesforce add-on covering Marketing Cloud. The exclusions point at unrelated UCs. The SPL's grouping cannot produce the per-campaign engagement rate the UC promises.
